newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE coffee dives to 31-month-low as funds sell.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE coffee dives to 31-month-low as funds sell.

text.p: Robusta coffee futures dived to a 31-month-low towards the close on Thursday, pounded by speculative and fund long liquidation.
Traders noted follow-through sales in the afternoon after benchmark January failed to come back towards the previous $1,360 support.
"Some locals who were long by the end of the day also got out of their positions as well," said a trader.
The second-position January plunged to an intraday low of $1,349 a tonne, the lowest level since April 15, 1994 when it touched $1,347.
But it barely recovered and ended the day at $1,352, a $38 loss. Heavy speculative selling earlier triggered sell-stops at just below $1,360.
New support is now seen at $1,315 area.
Traders said except for mounting concerns over prompt supplies there were little fresh fundamental inputs driving the market.
One trader said, "Basically, London has been over-valued for some time."
Spot month November also lost further ground, falling by a sharp $67 to $1,353 as longs liquidated some of the positions before the November expiry at lunchtime on Friday.
The sharp decline helped wipe out November's recent hefty premium to January.
Turnover was a moderate 7,564 lots, dominated by the January contract.
Jan/March switches saw deals at around $40.
